initial_regression_attempt.reason: 100ms benchmark asserted peak == slots; 20 runs completed successfully but 4 slots observed peak 2.
initial_regression_attempt.resolution: Benchmark verifies upper bound. New gated dispatcher tests independently prove saturation at 1, 2, 4 slots with one DB connection.

environment.model_wait: Gated async nodes in real LangGraph; two waiting runs held for at least 0.4s while real CRUD APIs execute.
environment.focused_checkpoint: InMemorySaver; existing real PostgreSQL saver tests also run in full suite

evidence: An intentionally held SELECT transaction causes a second checkout to time out at pool_size=1.
Two real queued Runs pass initial and HITL resume paths while CRUD C/R/U/D and Run GET use the same one-slot pool.
Actual cancel API works during gated graph execution and finalizes canceled without requiring recovery.
Task graph identity, messages and run logs persist; same-session new Run remains rejected.
Legacy prompt read closes before checkpoint update/invoke; stream projections close before next graph state and slow consumer.
Projection exception rolls back uncommitted writes; repeated cancellation waits for close/rollback and returns the connection.
Dispatcher fills 1, 2, 4 slots while the extra Run stays pending, then drains without claiming it.
limitations: Not a production pool size recommendation or a throughput/latency benchmark.
No global DB connection cap across replicas; existing pools/settings unchanged.
CRUD handler commits remain individually durable; no new atomicity across checkpoint and projection.
Recovery admin API deferred; uncertain-execution ownership protections remain.
No external LLM/Executor/Kubernetes load test; historical checkpoint_coexistence diagnostic not executed.
